text:
Barren County placed 39th among Kentucky counties for Project Based Section 8 assisted units in 2025
S. O. Wilson
Barren County placed 39th among 111 Kentucky counties in the 2025 Project Based Section 8 assisted-unit ranking, with 139 assisted units.
Barren County's Project Based Section 8 assisted-unit total was unchanged from 2024, staying at 139.
HUD-assisted housing programs typically lower rent for low-income households that meet eligibility requirements. HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households outlines three main categories of assistance: public housing, tenant-based assistance and privately owned, project-based assistance. Public housing is owned by local housing agencies, while tenant-based assistance, including housing vouchers, lets households lease homes in the private market. Project-based assistance is tied to specific privately owned properties with HUD rental-assistance contracts.
Households that receive HUD rental assistance typically pay 30% of their income after deductions toward rent, with the federal government covering the balance. Eligibility is based on HUD income limits that vary by location and household size, and applicants are commonly placed on waiting lists until assistance becomes available.
